20: Call me Ishmael. Some years ago, never mind how long precisely, having little or no money in my purse, and nothing particular to interest me on shore, I thought I would sail about a little and see the watery part of the world. It is a way I have of driving off the spleen and regulating the circulation, whenever it grows damp and drizzly.
24: 'You are a strange man,' said the stranger, turning toward me. 'Yet you speak like one who has known the sea.' I told him I had known it only from the shore, and that the sound of it at night had followed me inland for years. He nodded slowly, as though this were the answer he had expected, and said nothing more for a long while.
92: It is with considerable difficulty that I remember the original era of my being; all the events of that period appear confused and indistinct. 104: 'How long is it until sunrise?' I asked, and my own voice sounded thin in that enormous quiet. 'Three hours,' he answered, without consulting anything. 'Perhaps less. 140: Whenever I find myself growing grim about the mouth; whenever it is a damp, drizzly November in my soul; whenever I find myself involuntarily pausing before coffin warehouses, and bringing up the rear of every funeral I meet; then, I account it high time to get to sea as soon as I can. This is my substitute for pistol and ball.
147: 'Report,' the captain said, and the word carried further than he intended. 'There is nothing to report,' came the reply, faint and patient. 'I can see perhaps a hundred yards. 152: The thousand-and-first night dawned before the story was finished, and the teller, who had grown hoarse, asked leave to continue on the following evening. 183: 'You must not judge the place by its daylight,' the old man told me, filling my glass without being asked. 'Anyone can be brave at noon. 228: The palace of green porcelain, when we came to it, was in a ruinous state. The windows were broken, and the great doors stood open upon a hall of dust. Yet the tiles underfoot were as bright as the day they were laid, and where the light fell through the shattered roof they threw back a green so pure it seemed to come from beneath.
229: The city vanished from his sight, and the plain grey deck reassembled itself around him: the same rivets, the same worn rail, the same smell of oil and cold metal.
